#!/bin/sh
# >>> residual:pre-commit >>>
# residual pre-commit hook — validates residual/ data before commit
#
# Hard block: residual metadata must live on the git-sidecar branch, never on the
# working branch — except residual/config.toml, the in-repo pointer file. This check
# has no override flag by design.
LEAKED=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep '^residual/' | grep -v '^residual/config\.toml$')
if [ -n "$LEAKED" ]; then
  echo "residual: refusing commit — residual metadata staged on the working branch (belongs on the git-sidecar branch):" >&2
  echo "$LEAKED" | sed 's/^/  /' >&2
  echo "Unstage with: git restore --staged <path>" >&2
  exit 1
fi

STAGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep '^residual/')

if [ -z "$STAGED" ]; then
  STRICT=$(residual config 2>/dev/null | grep 'strict' | awk '{print $3}')
  [ "$STRICT" = "false" ] && exit 0
fi

residual verify all || exit 1
residual verify walk-reminder --staged || exit 1
# <<< residual:pre-commit <<<

The `residual view` redesign is done, tests pass (`nix build .#residual`, 340 total tests green), and changes are staged but not committed.

**What changed** (`src/view/html.rs` + `src/view/template.html`):
- The separate "Forces" list and component-chip list are gone; everything lives in one full-width matrix table (`calc(100vw - 4em)` × `calc(100vh - 5em)`), broken out of the page's padding so it doesn't cause horizontal page scroll.
- Sticky header row, sticky footer (column totals), sticky leftmost column (force), sticky rightmost column (row totals) — all four corners layered correctly (I caught and fixed a CSS specificity bug where a plain `.corner` class was losing to more specific sticky-row/sticky-col rules and would've let scrolling cells paint over the pinned corners).
- Force rows show as `S-<shortname>` / `P-<shortname>` accordion toggles; clicking expands a detail panel (description, naive-change, outcomes, attractor) inline — no separate list.
- Component headers get a status dot (proposed/actual/deprecated/other, styled distinctly) with a native tooltip explaining the stage.
- Column headers, the totals column, and the force column are all click-to-sort (asc/desc toggle).
- The filter bar is a sticky toolbar and now actually filters table rows (it only patched a force-list/component-chip pair before that's since been removed).
- Fusion/fission: a checkbox filters to candidate columns only, and a live range slider adjusts the fission threshold — both recomputed client-side from the rendered coupling cells, no server round-trip.

I verified the JS logic (sort, filter, accordion, fusion/fission threshold, the horizontal-overflow fix) against real project data (94 forces, 35 components) in a headless browser before the incident above — all behaved correctly. After that I switched to static/manual verification only, per your instruction.
